reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Department responsibility for injury prevention and brain injury services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 218/S.B. 125 & 341, A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Assigns responsibility for accessible injury prevention and brain injury rehabilitation, evaluation, coordination, treatment, and community support, qualified as subject to appropriations and wherever possible.

headings.title: Department powers, federal grants, and rulemaking duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (10) and history note. Covers brain injury planning with the advisory council, technical assistance, quality assurance, research, public information, nonstate cooperation, federal grant receipt/approval, charging/funding rules, participant-rights rules (199.001–199.051), and standard means-test rules.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Conditions effectiveness of rules under section 199.003 on compliance with chapter 536 and section 536.028, and voids rulemaking authority and post-August 28, 2011 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 3 (including subdivisions (1) to (10)), history note (L. 1991 H.B. 218/S.B. 125 & 341; A.L. 2011 H.B. 464), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Confirmed appropriations and "wherever possible" qualifications in subsection 1, adult brain injury charging/funding rule scope in 2(8), 199.001–199.051 cross-reference in 2(9), and chapter 536 / section 536.028 nonseverability with August 28, 2011 cutoff in subsection 3. Retained all three drafted titles.

headings.title: Direct or contracted injury prevention and brain injury services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 218/S.B. 125 & 341, A.L. 1993 H.B. 481, A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Authorizes ('may') direct or contracted delivery through Missouri public or private vendors using appropriated funds in the least restrictive environment close to the home community.

headings.title: Comprehensive traumatic brain injury service program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (15) and history note. Requires securing a comprehensive service program upon evaluation and request, qualified by available resources and federal/state law, listing nonexclusive services from assessment through supported work and long-term resource linkage.

headings.title: Participant involvement and least restrictive service setting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires involving the participant, family, or legal guardian in care and referral decisions and offering equal, appropriate services in the least restrictive setting close to the home community.

headings.title: Nondiscrimination in department-operated or funded programs and services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Prohibits denying admission or services in department-operated or funded programs based on race, sex, creed, marital status, national origin, handicap, or age, in accordance with state and federal law. Separate review: Revised title to reflect exact scope covering both department-operated and department-funded services or programs.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 4 (including subdivisions (1) to (15)), history note (L. 1991 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Confirmed permissive direct/contracted vendor delivery in subsection 1, traumatic brain injury scope and available-resources/request conditions in subsection 2, family/guardian involvement in subsection 3, and state/federal-law nondiscrimination scope in subsection 4. Revised subsection 4 title to cover both department-operated and funded programs and services; retained subsections 1 to 3.

headings.title: On-premises staff residence and monthly rental rates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 9379 through A.L. 1996 S.B. 540; Effective 7-1-96), and termination Revisor's Note (*Termination date 3-27-97). Describes archived DHSS-permitted on-premises staff housing and lower-of-cost-or-fair-market rent with director-approved exceptions without asserting post-1997 operation.

headings.title: Section termination after rehabilitation center transfer notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and Revisor's Note (*Termination date 3-27-97; notice received Feb. 25, 1997). Provides for section termination thirty days after Revisor notice of transfer of the Missouri rehabilitation center to the University of Missouri curators.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 and 2, history/prior-revision/effective notes (Effective 7-1-96), and termination Revisor's Note (*Termination date 3-27-97; transfer notice received February 25, 1997), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed DHSS permission and director-approved lower-rent exception in subsection 1 and thirty-day post-notice termination trigger in subsection 2 without implying post-1997 enforceability. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Charging and funding rules, public inspection, and University of Missouri exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 218/S.B. 125 & 341 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Directs chapter 536 rulemaking for charging and funding brain injury rehabilitation programs, requires public inspection at facilities, and exempts University of Missouri curator facilities, programs, and services. Separate review: Revised title to capture the public-inspection requirement alongside charging/funding rulemaking and the University of Missouri curators exemption.

headings.title: Rule compatibility standards and section 536.024 procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires rules and facility policies to match mission, population, size, and service type, and conditions chapter 199 rule effectiveness on promulgation under section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 and 2, history note (L. 1991 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Checked chapter 536 rulemaking scope, facility public-inspection requirement, University of Missouri curators exemption in subsection 1, and chapter-wide section 536.024 rule effectiveness condition in subsection 2. Revised subsection 1 title to include public inspection; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Receipt and administration of federal grants and aids
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 218/S.B. 125 & 341, A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Grants permissive ('may') authority to receive, administer, and pay out federal grants and aids for injury prevention and brain injury rehabilitation under grant terms.

headings.title: Approval of federal assistance applications after council consultation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the department director to approve advisable federal-assistance applications after consulting the Missouri brain injury advisory council.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 and 2, history note (L. 1991; A.L. 2011 H.B. 464), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Confirmed permissive ("may") federal grant receipt/administration under attached grant terms in subsection 1 and director approval after consulting the Missouri brain injury advisory council in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Confidentiality of facility and program patient records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective notes (L. 1991 H.B. 218 merged with S.B. 125 & 341; Effective 8-28-91 / 7-1-92). Classifies patient information and records compiled or maintained by department-operated or funded rehabilitation facilities or specialized programs as confidential.

headings.title: Mandatory record disclosures to specified requesters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and notes. Distinguished from subsection 3 by requiring ('shall disclose') disclosure upon request to a minor's parent, legal custodian/guardian, court-appointed attorney for listed wards/detainees, or patient-authorized attorney or physician. Separate review: Revised title from "upon authorized request" to "to specified requesters" because subdivisions (1) to (3) grant statutory request rights without patient authorization.

headings.title: Permissive record disclosures and recipient conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (8) and notes. Distinguished from subsection 2 by granting permissive ('may disclose') authority across eight categories, including patient-authorized, health-care, claims, de-identified research/audits, court administration (199.001–199.055), confidential law-enforcement/public-health, court/agency orders, and DSS abuse/neglect reporting. Separate review: Revised title to replace ambiguous "confidentiality limits" with "recipient conditions" covering de-identification in (4) and recipient confidentiality in (6).

headings.title: Required documentation of record disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires facilities or programs to document dates, nature, purposes, and recipients of all records disclosed under section 199.033.

headings.title: Preservation of judicial and administrative discovery rights
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Clarifies that section 199.033 does not limit discovery rights in judicial or administrative proceedings provided by statute or rule.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 5 (including subdivisions 2(1)–(4) and 3(1)–(8)), history and dual effective-date notes (Effective 8-28-91 H.B. 218; 7-1-92 S.B. 125 & 341), and verified all fingerprints. Checked mandatory versus permissive disclosure boundary, exact cross-references (chapter 632; sections 199.001 to 199.055), recipient confidentiality/de-identification conditions, documentation duty, and discovery preservation. Revised subsections 2 and 3 titles for requester and recipient-condition accuracy; retained subsections 1, 4, and 5.

headings.title: Probate court estate notice and means-test determination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 218/S.B. 125 & 341, A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Requires probate divisions aware of a patient's estate to notify the director, who applies the department's standard means test to determine whether to charge the estate.

headings.title: Conservator payment and permissive discharge for nonpayment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the conservator to pay notified estate charges and permits ('may') patient discharge after reasonable delay for nonpayment. Separate review: Revised title to make permissive ("may") discharge after reasonable delay explicit.

headings.title: Chapter 536 appeal, thirty-day discharge notice, and stay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Makes the director's decision final and appealable under chapter 536 in Cole County or the payer's county, requires thirty-day pre-discharge notice to conservator and court, and stays discharge pending appeal.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 3, history note (L. 1991; A.L. 2011 H.B. 464), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Confirmed probate-division notice and means-test application in subsection 1, conservator payment duty and permissive discharge after reasonable delay in subsection 2, and chapter 536 appeal venue (Cole County or payer's county), thirty-day pre-discharge notice, and automatic stay pending appeal in subsection 3. Revised subsection 2 title to make permissive discharge explicit; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Treatment and infection-control duties of tuberculosis patients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 518 § 2 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197). Requires a person found to have tuberculosis to follow local public health or department instructions, obtain required treatment, and minimize transmission risk.

headings.title: Petitions for DOT or commitment, venue, and pleading
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits local public health authorities to petition circuit court for DOT or commitment when an active-TB patient or potential transmitter exposes others after a compliance directive, setting venue and relaxed pleading rules. Separate review: Revised title to cover venue and relaxed pleading standards alongside permissive circuit court petitions for DOT or commitment.

headings.title: Ex parte petitions for emergency temporary commitment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits public health authorities to file an ex parte petition under section 199.200(5) when an active-TB patient or potential transmitter poses an immediate exposure threat.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 3, history note (L. 1961 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Confirmed patient duties in subsection 1, active-TB/potential-transmitter noncompliance trigger, permissive circuit court DOT or commitment petitions, venue, and relaxed pleading in subsection 2, and ex parte emergency commitment petitions under section 199.200(5) in subsection 3. Revised subsection 2 title to cover venue and pleading; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Hearing schedule, summons service, and certified exam reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 518 § 3 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197). Sets hearing five to fifteen days after petition filing, requires summons service at least three days prior, and admits certified X-ray and sputum reports without personal testimony. Separate review: Revised "certified lab evidence" to "certified exam reports" to cover both X-ray pictures and sputum examination reports; retained archived wording "report of any written report" without alteration.

headings.title: Legal representation for health authorities and respondents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Designates the prosecuting or city attorney to represent local public health authorities and directs court-appointed counsel for an indigent respondent upon request.

headings.title: County responsibility for court costs under 199.170 to 199.350
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Assigns proceedings costs under sections 199.170 to 199.350, including court-ordered exams but excluding respondent-procured exams, to the county where brought.

headings.title: Sheriff service and return of summons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs the county sheriff to serve summons and make return as in other civil cases for sections 199.170 to 199.350 proceedings.

headings.title: Ninety-six-hour emergency hearing, detention, and confinement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires a hearing within ninety-six hours of an ex parte section 199.180(3) petition, authorizes interim detention by the local health authority, and provides for section 199.230 confinement until a full hearing. Separate review: Revised title to include post-grant section 199.230 confinement pending full hearing alongside the ninety-six-hour hearing and interim detention.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 5, history note (L. 1961 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Checked hearing/summons timelines, admissibility of certified X-ray and sputum reports (noting archived wording "report of any written report"), counsel duties, county cost allocation excluding respondent-procured exams under 199.170–199.350, sheriff service, and ninety-six-hour emergency hearing, interim detention, and section 199.230 confinement. Revised subsections 1 and 5 titles for scope precision; retained subsections 2, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Respondent hearing rights and court-called witnesses or evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 518 § 4 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197). Protects respondent's rights to counsel, confrontation, cross-examination, and compulsory process, while permitting the court to call additional witnesses subject to cross-examination. Separate review: Revised title to include the court's discretionary authority to secure production of additional evidence as well as call witnesses.

headings.title: Commitment order, dismissal, custody, and transport costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs commitment to a DHSS-designated facility and sheriff transport upon public-health-danger findings (or dismissal otherwise), with transport costs paid from general county funds.

headings.title: Department care contracts and third-party payer exhaustion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes DHSS to contract for tuberculosis patient care, requiring state payment only after all third-party payer benefits are exhausted.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 3, history note (L. 1961 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Confirmed respondent confrontation/compulsory-process rights and court-initiated witnesses and evidence in subsection 1, potential-transmitter public-health-danger findings, commitment or dismissal, sheriff custody/delivery, and county transport costs in subsection 2, and permissive DHSS care contracts with third-party payer exhaustion in subsection 3. Revised subsection 1 title to include court-secured evidence; retained subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Facility contracts exempt from chapter 34 bidding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 518 §§ 10, 11 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197). Permits DHSS to contract for facilities necessary under sections 199.010 to 199.350 and exempts such contracts from chapter 34 competitive bidding.

headings.title: Third-party payer exhaustion for section 199.210 commitments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Restricts state payment for treatment and care of persons committed under section 199.210 until all third-party payer benefits are exhausted.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 and 2, history note (L. 1961 through A.L. 2013 S.B. 197), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Confirmed permissive DHSS facility contracting for sections 199.010 to 199.350 exempt from chapter 34 bidding in subsection 1 and third-party payer exhaustion prerequisite for section 199.210 commitments in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Unlawful acts and work exception for active tuberculosis
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note (L. 2013 S.B. 197). Prohibits persons knowingly infected with active pulmonary or laryngeal tuberculosis from reckless exposure without consent, reporting to work while contagious (except when adhering to treatment and deemed noninfectious), or violating commitment orders.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties and enhancement if victim contracts disease
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and Revisor footnote (*word 'subdivisions' appears in original rolls). Classifies subsection 1 violations as a class B misdemeanor, elevated to a class A misdemeanor if the victim contracts tuberculosis from the contact.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 (subdivisions (1) to (3)) and 2, history note (L. 2013 S.B. 197), and Revisor footnote (*word "subdivisions" appears in original rolls), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed knowing active pulmonary/laryngeal tuberculosis element, noninfectious-treatment work exception in 1(2), and class B misdemeanor / class A enhancement if victim contracts tuberculosis in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: CDC-based tuberculosis testing for health care workers and volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2013 S.B. 197). Requires tuberculin skin or IGRA testing upon employment and follow-up per latest CDC guidelines for health care facility employees and volunteers, without barring stricter institutional policies.

headings.title: Targeted campus testing programs and public health referrals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires Missouri higher education institutions to run targeted matriculation testing for on-campus students and faculty, with local public health referrals where no student health center exists.

headings.title: Enrollment bar for noncomplying entering higher education students
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Bars an entering higher education student who does not comply with the targeted testing program from maintaining enrollment in the subsequent semester.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Subjects section 199.290 rules to chapter 536 and section 536.028, and voids rulemaking authority and post-August 28, 2013 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1 to 4, history note (L. 2013 S.B. 197), and verified all source and body fingerprints. Checked CDC-guideline health care worker/volunteer testing and non-preemption of stricter institutional policies in subsection 1, higher education targeted campus testing and local public health referrals (199.170–199.350) in subsection 2, subsequent-semester enrollment bar limited to entering students in subsection 3, and chapter 536 / section 536.028 nonseverability (post-August 28, 2013) in subsection 4 (noting subsections 1 to 3 contain no separate express rulemaking delegation). Retained all four drafted titles.
